source_text: Inseris alia de libro meo verba, ubi dixi, "carnis inoboedientiam inoboedienti homini dignissime retributam; quia iniustum erat ut obtemperaretur a servo suo, id est a corpore suo, ei qui non obtemperaverat Domino suo" [n9] ; et conaris ostendere, "hanc inoboedientiam carnis potius esse laudabilem, si poena peccati est"; et tamquam persona sit aliqua, quae peccatorem scienter affligat, sic eam "velut ultricem sceleris, et in hoc Dei ministram", tamquam magum aliquod bonum cothurno sermonis exornas.
pass_a_gloss: You insert other words of mine from the book, where I said: 'the disobedience of the flesh to the disobedient man most worthily repaid; because it was unjust that by his servant, that is by his body, obedience be given to him who had not obeyed his own Lord'; and you strive to show 'this disobedience of the flesh rather to be praiseworthy, if it is punishment of sin'; and as if it were some person who knowingly afflicts the sinner, so you deck it out 'as avenger of crime, and in this God's minister', like some great good, with the tragic buskin of speech.

lemmas.gloss: tragic actor's boot; lofty, tragic style

pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “You insert other words from my book, where I said that ‘the disobedience of the flesh was most deservedly paid back to the disobedient human being, because it was unjust that he who had not obeyed his Lord should be obeyed by his servant, that is, by his body.’ And you try to show ‘that this disobedience of the flesh is rather to be praised, if it is the punishment of sin.’ And as though it were some person who knowingly afflicts the sinner, you adorn it in the high style of tragedy, as if it were some great good, ‘as an avenger of wickedness, and in this a servant of God.’”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: The transcription (augustinus.it, checked against the saved raw HTML) prints 'tamquam magum aliquod bonum'. Read as 'magnum' ('some great good'), taking 'magum' as a misprint; not checked against a Migne page image. A literal 'magus' ('like some good magician') would make poor sense with 'bonum'. Conjecture flagged for a human check.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
